transcript:
[Meeting header]
Date: 2027-01-05 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Arielle (Redwood AE), Markus (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood observer), Priya (Head of ML), Daniel (Platform), Sofia (Security), Amir (SRE)

[00:00] Arielle: thanks everyone for joining, really appreciate you making time. quick objective — today we want to map your p95 targets, peak concurrency windows and decide pilot path (hosted fast path vs dedicated or private).
[00:18] Priya: yeah thanks, we just spun up an evaluation internally. primary use case is streaming summarization for live customer transcripts, so low tail latency matters. our baseline with current infra is pretty bad during peaks, um.
[00:32] Daniel: to add, our infra team is concerned about cold starts and KV cache warmups, we see big p95 spikes after deploys.
[00:45] Markus: totally. curious — what p95 numbers are you aiming for? are we talking 200-300ms on streaming or more permissive?
[00:52] Priya: target is 350ms p95 for 128-token responses during peak, and about 50 concurrent streaming sessions. non-streaming batch responses can tolerate up to 1.2s p95.
[01:08] Arielle: ok that's helpful. rn our hosted profiles can hit ~300ms p95 for 128 token streams at moderate concurrency, but it depends on model selection, quant, and routing. our Dedicated offering gives more predictable p95 at scale because you reserve GPU pools.
[01:28] Amir: where does KV cache come in? we have a lot of repeated prefixes — can we avoid recomputing tokens?
[01:36] Markus: yes, we have prefix/KV caching. during streaming we keep the KV cache local to the serving shard; cache hits reduce end-to-end by 20-60% depending on prefix reuse. for burst scenarios the cache warm-up is the tricky part.
[01:55] Priya: so for a 50 concurrent user peak, what token/sec numbers should we expect?
[02:02] Markus: rough ballpark — for an Llama-2 style 13B quantized profile on our optimized runtime you might see ~70-120 tokens/sec sustained per GPU in streaming mode with low per-token overhead; but that's very workload dependent. if you have 50 concurrent streams generating 128 tokens each, peak token/s aggregate is about 50*128 / average latency window. the more important metric is tokens/sec delivered under p95 tail constraint.
[02:33] Daniel: can you translate that into how many GPUs or dedicated capacity we'd need? we run a budgeting exercise for commit levels.
[02:40] Arielle: yes — for the pilot we usually run a small poisson burst test. Markus, do you want to outline a sizing starting point?
[02:47] Markus: sure. with your target 350ms p95 for 128 tokens, assuming ~100 tokens/sec per GPU effective throughput, one GPU can service roughly 0.78 concurrent streams at that strict p95 if those streams are long lived — math is fuzzy because of batching. in practice we recommend a pool sized for steady-state concurrency plus headroom for 2x bursts and autoscale. for 50 concurrent, you'd likely reserve 60-80 GPU-equivalents of serving capacity unless you accept higher p95 during peaks.
[03:24] Priya: whoa that's higher than we expected — is that due to our strict p95?
[03:29] Markus: exactly — low p95 and streaming have higher per-connection costs because each token must be served quickly; batching helps but you can't batch too aggressively without hurting latency. another lever is model quantization and pruning to raise tokens/sec.
[03:45] Sofia: from security POV we need VPC, KMS integration and audit logs. Private deployment is attractive but has slower time-to-value. what are typical timelines?
[03:55] Arielle: Hosted: immediate, pilot in days; Dedicated: 2-6 weeks depending on sizing and procurement; Private (VPC with dedicated control plane or on-prem): 6-12+ weeks depending on network approvals and HSM/KMS gating.
[04:14] Amir: and SOC2? we need SOC2 plus fine-grained RBAC for multi-team access.
[04:21] Arielle: Redwood is SOC2 compliant and we can share the audit pack; RBAC and SSO/SAML integrations are standard in Dedicated and Private. we'll attach those docs.
[04:31] Priya: ok good. circling back to routing — can Redwood route lower-critical traffic to cheaper model variants during congestion? we'd like graceful degradation.
[04:41] Markus: yes, smart routing can route by policy: latency-first, cost-first, or hybrid. we can fallback to smaller quantized variants or even cached completions for repeat queries. there is an automatic fallback when capacity constrained.
[04:54] Daniel: how do we measure end-to-end p95? is it just server-side, or does Redwood provide token-level observability for client-side metrics?
[05:02] Markus: we provide token-level traces, per-request latency breakdown, and console dashboards with per-route p95 and cost. you can correlate user metrics with token counters.
[05:11] Priya: great. for our benchmark, we'd like Redwood to run three scenarios: steady-state 20 concurrent streams for 1hr, 50 concurrent burst for 10 minutes, and mixed batch+stream workload. can you also measure cold-start variance?
[05:25] Markus: yes we can. cold-starts are mostly for scaling events or new shard spin-up; dedicated reserved pools reduce cold-start frequency. we'll instrument tail latency histograms and share a CSV of per-interval tokens/sec and p50/p95/p99.
[05:40] Sofia: one security question — in Dedicated is customer data encrypted with our KMS keys?
[05:47] Arielle: yes, Dedicated supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM in Private, and Dedicated can also be configured with customer KMS depending on the cloud. we'll get you the specific cloud integration docs.
[05:59] Priya: what's the typical unit cost difference between Hosted and Dedicated for a sustained workload? we want to know break-even points.
[06:05] Arielle: Hosted has higher per-token rate but no commit; Dedicated lowers unit cost because you reserve capacity — the breakeven depends on utilization. we'll share a model spreadsheet. for a 24/7 workload with high utilization Dedicated almost always wins on cost.
[06:20] Daniel: on the benchmark harness, can you accept our real prompts — some are multi-turn and include function calls to our tools?
[06:28] Markus: yes we support function/tool calling scenarios; they affect token patterns and KV usage but are testable. include sample prompts and any expected structured output so we can measure correctness as well as latency.
[06:40] Priya: also, we have a regulatory window in EMEA — data residency matters. can Dedicated be region pinned?
[06:47] Arielle: yes, you can pin Dedicated pools to regions; Private gives the most control for on-prem or air-gapped.
[06:55] Amir: a practical question — if we go Hosted for the pilot and then move to Dedicated, how seamless is the migration?
[07:02] Markus: we keep consistent API and model catalog, and we support version pinning and rollouts. there may be config changes for networking and KMS, but code-level changes are minimal.
[07:14] Priya: ok sounds good. one more — what's your typical observed p95 degradation during autoscale events?
[07:21] Markus: autoscale can introduce short tail spikes, often in the sub-second to low-second range depending on model size. with Dedicated and enough headroom, those spikes are much smaller. we recommend autoscale thresholds tuned to your peak profile and some burst buffer.
[07:36] Jordan (interrupting): also worth noting our continuous batching logic attempts to fill micro-batches up to a latency SLO target to maximize tokens/sec; you can tune that target per-route.
[07:49] Priya: that tuning sounds crucial. for our benchmark we want sample SLOs for micro-batching to be 80ms per micro-batch — is that feasible?
[07:58] Markus: depends on model; some models have higher per-token compute. we can test micro-batching targets during the harness.
[08:06] Daniel: are there any quick wins to reduce required reserved capacity? e.g., more caching, model distillation, or routing to cached completions?
[08:15] Arielle: yes — prefix caching, increased quantization (fp16->int8), and routing repeated or low-value queries to cached completions give big wins. Also, moving non-critical workloads to off-peak windows and using adaptive batching policies helps.
[08:33] Sofia: and SLA? do you offer p95 SLAs on Dedicated?
[08:37] Arielle: yes, Dedicated has SLA-backed latency and uptime targets; specifics depend on contract tier. we'll include SLA bullets in the follow-up.
[08:45] Priya: ok let's recap next steps.
[08:48] Arielle: recap: Redwood runs the three scenario benchmark with Borealis prompts; Markus will provision harness; Arielle will send pricing and security docs; Borealis to confirm p95 windows, sample prompts and KMS details. schedule follow-up on 2027-01-13 to review results.
[09:05] Priya: that works, thanks everyone.
[09:08] Arielle: thanks all; we'll follow up with the links.
[09:12] [call ends]
